name: Impacket - Remote Command Execution (wmiexec/atexec/smbexec)
description: Execute commands / get a semi-interactive shell on Windows over different channels using valid creds or a hash. Pick the method by what's allowed and how stealthy you need to be.

variations.label: smbexec (SMB, semi-interactive, no Python on target)

notes: All need local-admin on the target. Stealth order (quiet->loud): wmiexec ~ atexec (no binary dropped) < smbexec < psexec (creates a service, event 7045). wmiexec/atexec run as the user; psexec gives SYSTEM. All accept -hashes for pass-the-hash. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 23 (Lateral Movement in Active Directory).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Lateral Movement in Active Directory

recommended.note: Validate which host the creds are local-admin on first.
Dump more hashes once you land.

examples.label: WMI exec into a DC with domain creds
Ch23 — wmiexec pass-the-hash with NT hash only (LM part left blank)

defense.why_it_works: Impacket exec tools (psexec, wmiexec, smbexec, atexec, dcomexec) run commands on a remote Windows host over SMB admin shares, WMI, DCOM, or the task scheduler using valid creds/hash/ticket.
defense.prerequisites: Valid credentials (password/hash/ticket) with admin rights on the target and the relevant service (SMB 445 / WMI / DCOM) reachable.
defense.impact: Remote command execution as the account - lateral movement to the target.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1021.002/T1047] psexec -> service creation (7045/4697) + ADMIN$ writes; wmiexec -> WMI process creation (Sysmon/Security 4688 with wmiprvse parent); 4624 type 3 + 4672; the semi-random output share/file.
defense.artifacts: A new service (psexec) or WMI-spawned process; ADMIN$/C$ writes; 4624/4672 logons; command output files.
defense.prevention: Restrict lateral admin (LAPS, tiering); block workstation-to-workstation SMB/WMI; monitor service creation (7045) and remote WMI; strong credential hygiene.
defense.evasion: wmiexec/atexec avoid the noisy service creation psexec makes; valid admin creds make logons look legitimate; clean up output files.
defense.misconfiguration: Credential material is accessible in multiple locations: SAM/NTDS.DIT via registry hives or VSS, LSASS minidump via Task Manager (non-admin on some configs), cached credentials in Windows Credential Manager (cmdkey), /etc/shadow readable by non-root. Offline attacks succeed because credentials are stored with weak hashing algorithms.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Windows Credential Manager stores cleartext/encrypted creds:
cmdkey /list
# Manages: Domain:interactive=CORP\svcaccount  (recoverable with DPAPI)

# /etc/shadow accessible (bad permissions):
ls -la /etc/shadow  # -rw-r--r-- 1 root shadow (group-readable)
# SHA-512 hashes: crackable with hashcat -m 1800
defense.secure_config:
# Windows: Credential Guard (prevents LSASS access)
# Audit Credential Manager entries:
cmdkey /list  # remove any unnecessary stored creds

# Linux /etc/shadow permissions:
chmod 640 /etc/shadow   # root:shadow only
chmod 400 /etc/shadow   # even stricter: root read-only

# Use yescrypt (default in Ubuntu 22+) instead of SHA-512:
# /etc/login.defs: ENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT  (memory-hard, much slower to crack)
# Existing hashes: force password reset to migrate

# Disable NTLM where possible (reduces hash theft value)
# Enforce Kerberos AES (makes captured hashes harder to crack)
